text.p: Italian debt markets started on a weaker footing following the overnight easier tone to U.S. Treasuries on some fears that the Federal Reserve may move soon to raise U.S. interest rates, dealers said.

The move by Treasuries pushed most European bonds into negative territory with bunds and gilts both easier. There was little fresh Italian domestic news and the BTP futures looked set to drift in rather directionless trade, they added.
"We had a poor lead from Treasuries and there seems little to push the market firmer today," said one trader on the LIFFE market in London.
Figures earlier today showed that Italy had a 451 billion lire trade surplus with non-European Union countries in January, had little overall market impact.
Background worries over a delay in EMU and concerns over political difficulties over the passage of the 1997 mini-budget are keeping many investors on the sidelines, dealers said.
"Again, it's largely a technical trading day with little sense of direction, with operators watching other markets for the next move," the LIFFE trader said.
